Every `! grep` in these Containerfiles is written as a build-time refusal and 46 of them failed nothing — they are mid-stanza, so their status is discarded and the build only ever stops if some LATER command in the same RUN fails. Found by the p1-063 lid agent in its own stanza; it wrote its refusals as `if ... exit 1` from the start and that is the idiom adopted. Ten of the 46 are not greps and were never in reach of the resolver at all: `apex-mux nonsense-verb`, `apex vm create --graphics spice`, `apex secret --help`, `apex recover reset` as root, `command -v qemu-system-x86_64` — all carrying real security decisions and asserting nothing. esp_ownership_2026_09_21.answer: NO. Windows-side installs boot systemd-boot like every other machine, and APEX BUILDS ITS OWN ESP rather than writing into Windows'. esp_ownership_2026_09_21.why_it_is_not_a_workaround: The 512 MiB problem was never about 512 MiB, it was about BORROWING. Squeezing into a partition Microsoft sized for Microsoft means competing with it forever: a feature update that grows \EFI\Microsoft reclaims the slack and the next apex update fails on a machine that worked yesterday. Owning the partition ends that class, and never opening Windows' ESP for writing is also the cheapest way to guarantee Windows' boot path survives byte-identical.
